description: The Ansob Center for Refugees (Ansob Center) has been providing immigration services since 2000. It will serve permanent residents from Arabic- and French-speaking countries in Africa and the Middle East residing in Astoria, Queens, New York. The Ansob Center was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2011. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, the Ansob Center will provide citizenship instruction to 200 lawful permanent residents (LPRs), administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 416 LPRs, and file 400 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Founded in 2015, the Asian Community Development Council (ACDC) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to educating, connecting, and empowering the Asian American and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (AANHPI) community in Nevada. ACDC will serve as the lead recipient for this project, collaborating with two other organizations, the Immigrant Home Foundation (IHF) and the College of Southern Nevada (CSN) to provide citizenship education and naturalization application services. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, ACDC and its partner organizations will provide citizenship instruction to 200 lawful permanent residents (LPRs), administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 270 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Aurora Comprehensive Community Mental Health Center, Inc.
description: Aurora Mental Health and Recovery’s (AMHR) Adult Education program (AE), formerly known as the Adult Education Department of the Asian Pacific Development Center (APDC), has a 20-year history of providing educational services to the adults most in need in Colorado. AMHR will serve as the lead recipient for this project, collaborating with Catholic Charities and Community Services of the Archdiocese of Denver, Inc. (Catholic Charities) to provide citizenship education and naturalization application services. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, AMHR and its partner organization will provide citizenship instruction to 200 lawful permanent residents (LPRs), administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Boat People SOS-Houston (BPSOS-Houston) has provided citizenship and English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction since 2009 through the Citizenship Initiative for Vietnamese Immigrant Communities (CIVIC) program. CIVIC aims to help Vietnamese and other LPRs overcome the multiple barriers to achieve citizenship through a rigorous bilingual curriculum for citizenship instruction and specialized legal expertise for naturalization application assistance. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, BPSOS-Houston will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Since its inception in 2011, the Burmese American Community Institute Inc. (BACI) has served more than 25,000 individuals. BACI collaborates with community partners such as refugee resettlement agencies to improve newcomers’ ability to navigate and understand the naturalization process and the U.S. legal system. BACI was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2019. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, BACI will provide citizenship instruction to 240 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 600 LPRs, and file 560 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Catholic Charities Bureau, Inc. (CCB) has been serving the Jacksonville area since 1975 with a mission to serve the most vulnerable, advocating for justice, human dignity, and quality of life. Beyond addressing immediate needs like food and housing, CCB supports refugees and newcomers through resettlement, ESL and immigration programs. To better serve the naturalization needs of future Americans in Northeast Florida, CCB’s adult education and immigration legal services programs will provide citizenship classes and naturalization applications services to LPRs. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, CCB will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 225 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N- 400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston
description: Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston has been providing immigration legal services since the inception of the St. Frances Cabrini Center for Immigrant Legal Assistance. Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston/Houston is partnering with Center for Career Transformation which has been providing citizenship instruction since 2018. Catholic Charities of Galveston-Houston in partnership with Center for Career Transformation aims to provide a continuum of service to support immigrants yearning to become citizens. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and its partner organization will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 205 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Roman Catholic of the Diocese of Rochester
description: Catholic Charities Diocese of Rochester’s Catholic Charities Family and Community Services (CCFCS) has served the Greater Rochester community since 1917. CCFCS has been administrating citizenship programming including ESL/civics instruction and naturalization assistance consistently since 2013 and was awarded its first USCIS grant in FY 2015. The presence of many refugees and immigrants in Rochester and the Finger Lakes area drives the continued need for citizenship and integration services provided by CCFCS. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, CCFCS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 300 LPRs, and file 260 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Syracuse
description: Catholic Charities of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Syracuse, DBA Catholic Charities of Onondaga County (CCOC) received its first USCIS grant in 2018 which focused on the vulnerable immigrant population as part of its Refugee Resettlement Services. Currently, an influx of Afghan asylees are present in its area. CCOC implemented ESL instruction and citizenship instruction in 2011 and 98% of its students have passed the naturalization exam. CCOC will enroll at least 200 students and file 200 N-400s during the FY24 grant cycle.

Catholic Migration Services (CMS) and its partner, LaGuardia Community College (LGCC), have more than 60 years of combined experience providing immigration and education services to its immigrant population in Brooklyn and Queens. The LPR population originates from two dozen nations in Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia and Europe. LGCC will provide ESL and citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs during the two-year grant period while CMS’ robust legal team will provide 200 N-400 screenings and 200 N-400 filings.

organization_name: Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc.
description: The Center for Pan Asian Community Services, Inc. of Georgia (CPACS) has more than 40 years of experience providing services to the refugee and immigrant population in the state of Georgia. The LPR population hails from a variety of countries of origin such as Korea, China and Vietnam as well as countries in Latin America and Africa. During the last 15 years, CPACS has offered citizenship instruction and approximately 90% of its students have passed the naturalization test. In addition to its successful citizenship instruction program, CPACS has provided immigration consultation and naturalization services for more than 25 years. During the FY24 grant cycle, CPACS plans to serve more than 200 new students and file more than 200 N-400s.

Founded by refugees in 1981, the Chinese Mutual Aid Association (CMAA) serves the needs, promotes the interests, and enhances the well-being of diverse immigrant and refugee communities across Metropolitan Chicago. CMAA accomplishes its mission through social services, advocacy, educational programming, and assistance for clients of all ages. With their wraparound service model and offices in Uptown Chicago, West Ridge, and Elgin, CMAA serves over 5,000 clients annually in Cook and Kane counties. CMAA is a trusted citizenship service provider for diverse immigrant populations, with specialized expertise in serving Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) communities. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, CMAA will provide citizenship instruction to 140 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 250 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Sponsors Organized to Assist Refugees (SOAR), a program of Ecumenical Ministries of Oregon (EMO) is located in Portland, Oregon. Founded in 1979, SOAR's mission is to assist refugees in becoming self-sufficient, integrated community members. SOAR’s legal program began in 1992 and has been recognized by the Department of Justice since 1995. SOAR provides culturally competent immigration-related legal representation and education to Oregon's lower income refugees and immigrants. SOAR began the New Americans Initiative (NAI) in 2010 and has provided comprehensive citizenship services ever since. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, EMO will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 250 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Immigrant Law Center of Minnesota, Inc.
description: The Immigrant Law Center of Minnesota (ILCM) and sub-awardee, Literacy Minnesota (LM) have worked together to provide citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to immigrants since 2013. Their primary clients are LPRs living in rural Minnesota, as well as the Latinx, Somali, Hmong, and Karen communities of Minneapolis and St. Paul. ILCM and LM were first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2013. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, ILCM and LM will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 224 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

International Institute of Metropolitan Detroit (IIMD) will serve the needs of southeast Michigan’s diverse LPR communities. It will offer citizenship classes at three community sites, in the heart of densely populated immigrant neighborhoods within the Detroit Metropolitan area serving LPRs of Hispanic, Middle Eastern, Syrian, Yemi, and European. In addition, IIMD will provide one virtual citizenship class for the remote tri-county area and beyond, reaching LPRs from diverse countries such as Iraq, China, India, Bangladesh, Yemen, Nigeria, Senegal and Egypt. With USCIS FY2024 grant funding, IIMD will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 245 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Immigration Institute of the Bay Area
description: The Immigration Institute of the Bay Area (IIBA) has been providing ESL/citizenship classes since 1983, totaling 41 years of educational experience. IIBA obtained Department of Justice (DOJ) recognition in 1958 and will provide comprehensive naturalization legal services to immigrant communities in the San Franciso Bay Area. With USCIS FY2024 grant funding, IIBA will provide citizenship instruction to 210 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 210 LPRs, and file 210 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The International Institute of Minnesota (IIMN) in Saint Paul, Minnesota has been a cornerstone of the Twin Cities community since 1919, providing essential services, including English classes, to refugees and immigrants. IIMN is partnering with sub-awardee Southeast Minnesota Adult Basic Education Consortium (Southeast ABE) to provide citizenship instruction services and naturalization application services in Austin, Albert Lea, Winona, Owatonna, and Faribault, Minnesota. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, IIMN and Southeast ABE will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 218 LPRs, and file 210 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Jewish Vocational Service of MetroWest, Inc.
description: JVS of MetroWest has been providing comprehensive vocational services since 1939. Annually, JVS helps over 4,500 individuals overcome barriers to employment related to age, ability, education, immigrant status, job skills, and language. JVS emphasizes immigrant integration through its refugee services, English as a Second Language (ESL) classes, citizenship classes, ABE classes, job skills training programs with ESL components, and career guidance and placement, which collectively help approximately 1,000 immigrants and refugees annually. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, JVS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Journey’s End Refugee Services (JERS) in Buffalo, NY has been offering comprehensive English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction since 2010 and began offering citizenship preparation classes in 2019. Their lawful permanent resident (LPR) student population includes refugees, asylees, and immigrants. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, JERS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Lancaster-Lebanon Intermediate Unit 13 (IU13) is an educational service agency providing classes and services for children, youth, and adults in Lancaster and Lebanon Counties. IU13’s Community Education programs have served Lancaster and Lebanon’s adult ESL students since 1971. IU13 will serve as the lead applicant for this project, collaborating with the Church World Service (CWS) to provide naturalization application services. CWS has provided legal services in the Lancaster community for 18 years and provides naturalization services to a diverse LPR population that includes former refugees, asylees, diversity visa recipients, and LPRs who arrived via family petition. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, IU13 and CWS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The Literacy Center of West Michigan (Literacy Center) is partnering with sub-awardee Lighthouse Immigrant Advocates (LIA) to provide citizenship preparation services and naturalization application services in western Michigan. The Literacy Center began offering citizenship preparation classes in 2019 primarily to immigrants from Mexico, Honduras, and Burma. Currently, the top three countries of origin for Literacy Center leaners are Mexico, Guatemala, and Burma. Literacy Center has previously been awarded a USCIS grant. LIA has been providing naturalization application services since 2016. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, the Literacy Center and LIA will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Since 1979, Literacy New Jersey (Literacy NJ), has been committed to strengthening New Jersey’s workforce, families, and communities by ensuring free, high-quality ESL instruction is available to adults who struggle with literacy. Literacy NJ serves primarily hard-to-reach LPRs, who earn low incomes, as well as those who identify as a member of a marginalized community. Literacy NJ and their partner Puerto Rican Action Board will offer an expansion of citizenship instruction and naturalization services to LPRs throughout New Jersey. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, Literacy NJ and the Puerto Rican Action Board will provide citizenship instruction to 140 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 140 LPRs, and file 140 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Lutheran Services in Iowa (LSI) has been providing services to resettled immigrants and refugees in Central Iowa for over four decades. LSI will serve as the lead application for this project, collaborating with Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice (IMMJ). IMMJ has been providing immigration legal services for the past 23 years in Central Iowa and the entire state. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, LSI and IMMJ will provide citizenship instruction to 228 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 220 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Lutheran Social Services of South Dakota
description: Lutheran Social Services of South Dakota (LSSSD) has been providing citizenship education since 2010 and immigration legal services since 1994. With FY 2024 grant funding, LSSSD will primarily service Sioux Falls, Yankton, and Aberdeen, South Dakota and surrounding areas. These cities have all experienced significant growth in the number of residents who are not U.S. Citizens. Naturalization Services may also be provided for individuals in other areas of South Dakota, as well as neighboring communities in southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The primary countries of origin of LPRs to be served by LSSSD are Liberia, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Sierra Leone, Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, Burma, Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Philippines, Ukraine, Bosnia, Iraq, Mexico, Cuba, Canada, and other Central American, Southern American and European countries. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, LSSSD will provide citizenship instruction to 220 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 500 LPRs, and file 250 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition, Inc.
description: The Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition (MIRA) and St. Mark Community Education Program (SMCEP) will offer a joint program that provides both citizenship instruction and naturalization application services. SMCEP has a long history of providing citizenship preparation instruction, while MIRA has been offering application assistance for more than a decade. Having already successfully collaborated through the FY22 CINAS grant and before that informally for some time, this project will allow the organizations to further integrate their services and assist eligible individuals to prepare and apply for naturalization. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, MIRA and SMCEP will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The Polish American Association (PAA) has been providing citizenship instruction for 25 years and naturalization application services for more than 34 years to Polish and other immigrant communities settling in Metro Chicago. With USCIS FY 2024 grant funding, PAA will ensure at least 200 LPRs with limited-English gain sufficient mastery of English, American history, culture, and government to apply for U.S. Citizenship. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, PAA will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 220 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Pomona Economic Opportunity Center, Inc. (PEOC) has been an advocate for its hard-to-reach immigrant community since 1998. In 2022, PEOC introduced much needed ESL and citizenship classes to a diverse LPR population from countries such as Mexico, Tonga, Bangladesh and elsewhere. Additionally, PEOC has offered naturalization application assistance since 2015. With FY24 CIGP funding, PEOC plans to expand its reach by enrolling a minimum of 180 LPRS in citizenship class and file 180 Form N-400s.

Progreso Latino, Inc. is the fiscal agent for the Rhode Island Citizenship Consortium, a group of five non- profit agencies serving the immigrant community. The Consortium agencies are strategically located in Providence County and the cities of Providence, Central Falls, Pawtucket, East Providence and Cranston. With FY24 funding, Progreso Latino intends to serve over 350 students, to conduct over 400 N-400 screenings and to file 400 Form N-400s.

Quincy Asian Resources, Inc. (QARI) has been providing immigration services since 2001. QARI’s mission is to foster and improve the social, cultural, economic, and civic lives of immigrants and their families to benefit their communities. QARI will serve lawful permanent residents residing in Quincy and neighboring towns on the South Shore. With USCIS FY 2024 grant funding, QARI will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screening to over 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Located in the heart of the Central Shenandoah Valley of Virginia, Skyline Literacy, a community-based, non-profit organization, has been providing literacy services since 1987 to adult residents of Harrisonburg and Rockingham County, with over 31 years of experience providing adult ESL instruction (1993 to present). Church World Service (CWS) Harrisonburg provides the naturalization application services. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, Skyline Literacy and CWS will provide citizenship instruction to 160 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 160 LPRs, and file 160 Forms N- 400 and G-28.

The International Rescue Committee Boise (IRC) is the largest refugee resettlement agency in Idaho. IRC opened its Boise office in 2005 and has more than twelve years of experience providing naturalization application services. IRC will serve as the lead applicant for this project, collaborating with the English Language Center (ELC) to provide citizenship instruction. ELC has been providing English language instruction for newly arrived refugees in Idaho since 1999. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, IRC and ELC will provide citizenship instruction to 160 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 160 LPRs, and file 160 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The International Rescue Committee in Charlottesville (IRC Charlottesville) has more than 25 years’ experience providing services to refugee and immigrant populations and has been offering immigration legal services for refugees and other immigrants since 2002. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, IRC Charlottesville, in collaboration with Literacy Volunteers of Charlottesville/Albemarle (LVCA), will provide citizenship instruction to 120 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 120 LPRs, and file 120 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The International Rescue Committee, Inc., in Wichita (IRC Wichita) provides low cost-immigration legal assistance to immigrants in the state of Kansas. Each year in Sedgewick County, IRC Wichita submits approximately 800 immigration applications to USCIS. As demand is high for citizenship services, the office will carry out successful and recurrent citizenship instruction and naturalization and integration services within the lawful permanent resident (LPR) community. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, IRC Wichita will provide citizenship instruction to 160 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 160 LPRs, and file 160 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: The University of North Carolina at Greensboro
description: The University of North Carolina at Greensboro’s New Arrivals Institute (NAI) is a non-profit organization whose mission is to assist refugees and immigrants with self-sufficiency and U.S. citizenship through education. Incorporated in 2010, NAI has provided services to over 7,000 refugees and immigrants. NAI collaborates with local service providers and community partners to provide clients with the tools, skills, and knowledge they need to integrate and attain self-sufficiency. NAI blends in-house expertise with partnerships to ensure that services meet the needs of refugees and immigrants with English classes, cultural orientation, citizenship preparedness, health literacy, vocational education, skills recertification, and parent orientation. With USCIS FY 2024 funding, NAI will provide citizenship instruction to 256 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 320 LPRs, and file 280 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The Young Women’s Christian Association of Tulsa (YWCA Tulsa) has received funding from USCIS since 2009. It has more than 40 years’ experience serving immigrants and refugees, with 4,000 served annually. Its clients originate from more than 60 countries but are primarily from Central and South America, Burma, and the former Soviet Union. There are approximately 10,000 eligible LPRs in the Tulsa area and the YWCA is positioned to provide both citizenship instruction and naturalization application services. It plans to enroll 200 students and provide naturalization services to 200 LPRs during the 2024 grant cycle.

organization_name: World Relief Corporation of National Association of Evangelicals
description: The World Relief Corporation of the National Association of Evangelicals has partnered with Modesto Junior College (MJC) to offer citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to address its needs in the Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) community. There are approximately 27,000 LPRs in and around Stanislaus County, predominantly from Mexico, Central and South America, as well as a recent influx of refugees hailing from Afghanistan, Syria and Ukraine. World Relief is an experienced immigration legal service provider since 1987 while Modesto College has offered citizenship instruction since the 1980’s. Together, the organizations plan to provide classes and file Form N-400s and G-28s for 120 LPRS with the FY24 grant. Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA)

Catholic Charities of Southeast Michigan (“CCSEM”) serves the six-county region of southeastern Michigan. Reflecting a profound respect for human life and a commitment to enhance family life, Catholic Charities of Southeast Michigan (CCSEM) provides a wide variety of services, annually assisting more than 20,000 people of all faiths, races, and cultures. CCSEM has 12 locations serving residents in six counties. CCSEM was formed as a 501(c)(3) in 2012 through the voluntary merger of five county-based Catholic social services organizations. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, CCSEM aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming and naturalization application services for LPRs in its six-county region.

Catholic Charities of Louisville (CCL) was founded in 1939 primarily as an adoption services provider. Today CCL provides a range of programs and services ranging from refugee resettlement to food pantries to community gardening to indigent burial, serving 46,125 clients in the previous calendar year. Catholic Charities of Louisville’s (CCL) Migration and Refugee Services (MRS) has been resettling refugees in the Louisville, Kentucky area since the mid-1970s. In addition, CCL has an in-house Immigration Legal Services (ILS) program which has since 1992 assisted those who need quality, lower-cost assistance with services such as permanent residence, family reunification, citizenship, naturalization, and more. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, CCL aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming for LPRs in the Louisville area.

Founded in 1978, Immigration Counseling Service (ICS) is Oregon’s oldest, and only, independent non- profit law firm providing legal services to low-income immigrants across the state. As most immigration legal service and citizenship preparation providers are based solely in the Portland metro area, rural and low-income immigrant communities often lack access to these vital services. Over the next three years, ICS will develop new citizenship programs in Oregon, with an emphasis on underserved rural areas. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, ICS aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming for LPRs across rural Oregon.

The International Rescue Committee Denver (IRC Denver) strives to address the critical need for citizenship services among LPRs in the Denver metro and greater Front Range areas. Serving nearly 6,000 refugees, Special Immigrant Visa (SIV) recipients, asylees, and other immigrants since 2016, IRC Denver provides wraparound services aimed at supporting stability and long-term integration for its clients. Colorado is home to 160,929 LPRs, with over 125,000 eligible for naturalization. The Denver metro and greater Front Range areas house the majority of these eligible LPRs, many of whom face significant barriers to naturalization, such as high application costs, language proficiency issues, and limited access to legal and educational support. With only 12% of eligible LPRs in Denver considered to have a high probability of naturalizing, the IRC’s participation in the CITA program addresses a pressing need for accessible citizenship services. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, IRC Denver aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming and naturalization application services for LPRs in the Denver metro and greater Front Range areas.

Justice for Our Neighbors – Nebraska, doing business as Immigrant Legal Center + Refugee Empowerment Center (ILC+REC), has 10 offices stretching across the state of Nebraska and southwestern Iowa. ILC+REC is the largest federally recognized refugee resettlement agency in the state of Nebraska, and the largest provider of high quality, pro bono immigration legal services in the region. ILC+REC's mission is to empower immigrants and refugees to live confidently through high-quality legal representation, refugee resettlement, and social work services. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, ILC+REC aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming to address this growing need in Omaha-Council Bluffs.

Established in 1993, South Texas College (STC) is a public institution of higher education located in McAllen, TX, serving Hidalgo and Starr Counties. The LPR community’s primary country of origin is Mexico, with some LPRs from India, the Philippines, and El Salvador. STC’s mission is to provide educational opportunities through excellence in teaching and learning, workforce development, cultural enrichment, community service, and regional and global collaborations. STC’s vision is to be a global model in educational innovation serving as a catalyst to drive regional prosperity, economic development, and the social mobility of those they serve. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, STC’s Continuing Education and Workforce Development Department aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming for LPRs across its service area.

World Relief Quad Cities’ (WRQC) main office is in Moline, Illinois, with a secondary office in Davenport, Iowa. WRQC's goals are to provide financial, emotional, cultural, and spiritual support to refugees – victims of war and persecution from around the world – who seek refuge in the Quad Cities area. WRQC has worked with the local refugee population and broader immigrant community for over 25 years. Through the Citizenship and Integration Training Academy (CITA) program, WRQC aims to develop comprehensive citizenship education programming to serve select LPR communities with the greatest need in Illinois and Iowa.

organization_name: 1199 SEIU League Training and Upgrading Fund
description: Founded in 1969, the 1199 SEIU League Training and Upgrading Fund (TUF) is an organization that provides a full array of education benefits to healthcare workers. Since its 2001 creation, the 1199 SEIU Citizenship Program has helped nearly 14,000 healthcare workers obtain U.S. citizenship. To date, TUF has provided citizenship education for nearly 9,000 lawful permanent residents (LPRs). Through this grant, TUF will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and naturalization application services to 200 LPRs.

Access California Services has been providing immigration services since 2007. It will serve lawful permanent residents from across the globe, but with a focus on clients from Arabic, Urdu, Farsi, and Pashtu speaking countries who reside in Southern California. Access California Services was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2012. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, Access California Services will provide citizenship instruction to 250 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 300 LPRs, and file 250 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Asian Counseling and Referral Service (ACRS) was established in 1973 and assists over 30,000 primarily Asian and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander immigrants and refugees annually through multiple culturally competent social and health programs with 315 staff who speak over 40 languages and dialects. ACRS has over 26 years of experience providing citizenship instruction and naturalization application services and has been accredited through the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) since 2005. Under the FY 2023 grant cycle, ACRS will provide citizenship instruction to 220 LPRs and naturalization application services to 300 LPRs.

organization_name: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans
description: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans (CCANO), a 501c3 faith-based non-profit organization, has been a USCIS grant recipient since 2017. CCANO anticipates enrolling 200 students in citizenship instruction courses, providing naturalization eligibility screenings for over 200 LPRs, and filing an estimated 200 Forms N-400 and G-28 for eligible LPRs. They will also 1 provide naturalization case management and application assistance by DOJ-accredited representatives.

organization_name: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of San Antonio, Inc.
description: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of San Antonio (CCAOSA), in partnership with the San Antonio Independent School District’s (SAISD) Adult & Community Education Program will provide English as a Second Language (ESL) and citizenship instruction classes, as well as free legal representation for clients in pursuit of naturalization. SAISD will provide multi-level classes during varying time slots. To provide a multitude of options to those in San Antonio and Del Rio, Texas, classes will be held in-person and online. Caritas Legal Services will help clients navigate the naturalization process. Attorneys can provide their services in multiple languages including Spanish, Arabic, Amharic, Hindi, Oromo, Pashto, Dari, and Somali. During their naturalization process, clients will be kept informed of their progress and provided extra resources through "Ask-A-Lawyer" events and mock interviews. In the FY 2023 grant cycle, CCAOSA will provide citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to 200 individuals.

Catholic Charities' Migration and Refugee Service (MRS) has partnered with community-based organization Building Hope in the City (BHITC) to provide citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to individuals residing in Northeast Ohio. Together, the organizations will serve 240 participants in each of the grant components.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas, Inc.
description: Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas (CCNEK), a community faith-based organization, has provided English as a second language instruction for more than 38 years, teaching over 9,000 immigrants how to read, write, and speak English. In 2010, CCNEK established La Luz Center for Immigration Legal Assistance which provides low-cost professional immigration legal services. In 2015, the CCNEK Citizenship Preparation Program (CPP) began offering citizenship classes. During the past eight years, CPP has had nearly 1,000 enrollees receive citizenship instruction. It is anticipated that with FY 2023 grant funding, CCNEK will provide citizenship instruction to 240 LPRs and provide naturalization application services to 270 LPRs.

For more than 15 years, Catholic Charities of Northern Nevada (CCNN) has been providing a full range of immigration legal services. CCNN is the largest, most diverse program of its kind in Northern Nevada. In response to the ever-growing unmet needs for legal representation in immigration matters within their region, CCNN has expanded its Immigration Legal Services 2 (ILS) to provide an even greater focus on naturalization applications. CCNN is partnering with Northern Nevada Literacy Council (NNLC) to provide language and citizenship education under this program. The course instruction, training materials, textbooks, and handouts will be provided to students at no cost. Naturalization application services and citizenship instruction will be provided at no cost to low income LPRs throughout Northern Nevada. For the FY 2023 grant cycle, they will enroll at least 200 students, provide at least 200 Form N-400 screenings, and file at least 200 Forms N-400.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of Southwest Kansas, Inc.
description: Catholic Charities of Southwest Kansas (CCSWKS) serves LPRs in southwest Kansas and northwest Oklahoma. Under the FY 2023 grant cycle, CCSWKS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and provide naturalization application services to 200 LPRs. Citizenship instruction will be provided at three sites: Dodge City Community College, Garden City Community College, and Seward County Community College. Naturalization application services will be provided by CCSWKS in Great Bend, Dodge City, and Garden City, KS.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Santa Rosa
description: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Santa Rosa has provided immigration services since 1975. It will serve permanent residents from Spanish, Khmer, Tagalog, and Tigrinya-speaking countries residing in Sonoma, Mendocino, Humboldt, Del Norte, and Lake. Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Santa Rosa was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2014. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Santa Rosa will provide citizenship instruction to 210 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 240 LPRs, and file 210 Forms N- 400 and G-28s.

organization_name: Catholic Charities San Bernardino and Riverside Counties
description: Catholic Charities of San Bernardino and Riverside counties has provided immigration services since 1992. Catholic Charities of San Bernardino and Riverside will serve permanent residents from primarily Spanish-speaking countries residing in San Bernardino and Riverside counties. The organization was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2016. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, Catholic Charities of San Bernardino and Riverside counties will provide citizenship instruction to 225 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 340 LPRs, and file 225 Forms N- 400 and G-28.

Central American Resource Center (CARECEN-DC) has provided immigration services since 1981. It will serve lawful permanent residents from primarily Spanish-speaking and other 3 countries residing in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan area. CARECEN-DC was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2016. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, CARECEN-DC will provide citizenship instruction to 300 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 300 LPRs, and file 300 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Central American Resource Center of California
description: Central American Resource Center (CARECEN) of California has provided immigration services since 1983. It will serve lawful permanent residents from Spanish-speaking countries, primarily those residing in Los Angeles County. CARECEN of California was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2017. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, CARECEN of California will provide citizenship instruction to 240 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 600 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Since 1995, the DOJ-recognized organization Chinese American Service League –(CASL), has created a pathway through U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to help LPRs prepare for citizenship and become engaged U.S. citizens, ready to exercise their rights and responsibilities. For over 28 years, CASL has provided ESL and citizenship classes to more than 5,850 LPRs, and has provided naturalization application, legal consultation, case management, and interpretation services to over 1,235 LPRs annually. Under the FY 2023 grant, the organization will provide citizenship instruction, naturalization eligibility screenings, and file Forms N-400 and G-28 for 180 LPRs.

The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) has been providing immigration services since 2007. It will serve permanent residents from Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego, Mountain View, San Jose, Alameda, and Sacramento counties of California. CHIRLA was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2021. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, CHIRLA will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Community Action Board of Santa Cruz County, Inc.
description: Since 1986, Community Action Board of Santa Cruz County has provided immigration services to permanent residents residing in Monterey, San Benito and Santa Cruz Counties. Community Action Board of Santa Cruz County was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2021. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, Community Action Board of Santa Cruz County will provide citizenship 4 instruction to 240 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 240 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The Community Center for Immigrants Incorporated (CCI) will offer citizenship preparation services to LPRs in the Milwaukee, WI metropolitan area, including the growing refugee community. Milwaukee has the largest Burmese Rohingya population in the United States; in the past year, 60% of CCI’s students were Burmese Rohingya refugees. Thus, CCI has tailored its citizenship instruction program to meet the unique needs of refugee learners. CCI will also provide naturalization application services through its DOJ-accredited representative. Additionally, CCI will use the USCIS grant funding to expand the number of employees with accredited representative status. In the FY 2023 grant cycle, CCI will provide citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to 200 individuals.

organization_name: Edith and Carl Marks Jewish Community House of Bensonhurst
description: Edith and Carl Marks Jewish Community House (JCH) of Bensonhurst was founded in 1927 to serve as a community center for Eastern European Jewish immigrants. Most recently, JCH has supported 5,100 Ukrainian refugees with resettlement services. Additionally, JCH offers a variety of other social services, including citizenship instruction, and naturalization legal services for all immigrants in its area. JCH proposes to serve 120 LPRs under the FY 2023 CINAS grant.

Emerald Isle Immigration Center (EIIC) has provided naturalization services since 1988. EIIC’s citizenship instruction program began in 2006 as a casual grassroots initiative. EIIC first received USCIS grant funding in FY 2011. The immigrant community they serve comes from all five boroughs of New York City and the counties just north and east, with the majority residing in Queens, Brooklyn, and the Bronx. For the FY 2023 grant cycle, EIIC will enroll 560 students, provide 400 Form N-400 screenings and file 320 N-400 applications with G-28s.

Since the 1980’s, the Fresno Unified School District has provided immigration services. Fresno Unified School District serves permanent residents from all countries; however, the majority of their constituents are primarily Spanish, Hmong, and Punjabi-speaking residents residing in Fresno County. Fresno Unified School District was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2012. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, the Fresno Unified School District will provide citizenship 5 instruction to over 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to over 350 LPRs, and file a minimum of 240 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Friendly House provides citizenship preparation services for lawful permanent residents and opportunities for immigrants to integrate into American society. In the past five years, Friendly House has provided more than 2,000 LPRs with ESL and citizenship instruction. The program provides support to immigrants from diverse backgrounds so that they can make successful transitions into their new home. Friendly House proposes to expand and enhance its citizenship services by providing 200 unduplicated LPRs with citizenship instruction and 200 LPRs with naturalization application services in Maricopa County.

Hartford Public Library’s (HPL) division for Adult Education and Immigrant Services known as The American Place (TAP) serves as a hub for ESL and citizenship instruction, Green Card renewal, legal services and other robust support programs needed to achieve U.S. citizenship. The City of Hartford is a significant immigrant gateway, with current arrivals originating from many parts of the world, particularly the West Indies, Latin America, as well as India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. HPL has been a USCIS grantee since 2010 and for the FY 2023 grant cycle, it projects it will serve a minimum of 204 individuals with citizenship instruction and file 375 N- 400s.

organization_name: HIAS Council and Migration Service of Philadelphia
description: Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society of Pennsylvania (HIAS PA), a lead agency in the Philadelphia Citizenship Action Network (P-CAN), has been a USCIS grant recipient for 10 years. Through its P-CAN partnerships, HIAS PA will serve the diverse LPR community’s unmet needs by offering high-quality, free citizenship instruction and naturalization application assistance. HIAS PA expects to enroll 220 new students, screen 350 LPRs for naturalization eligibility and file 200 N-400s during the FY 2023 grant cycle.

Since 1977, Instituto del Progreso Latino (Instituto) has supported Hispanic immigrants and their families on the Southwest Side of Chicago. Through its Fast Track to Citizenship program, an ESL and naturalization service initiative, Instituto will offer citizenship instruction to beginning and intermediate level English speaking LPRs. Instituto was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2011. With FY 2023 grant funding, Instituto plans to enroll 420 permanent residents in citizenship classes and provide 600 permanent residents with naturalization application services. 6

organization_name: InterFaith Works of Central New York
description: Since 1976, InterFaith Works of Central New York (IFW) has provided ESL and citizenship instruction to the immigrant community in Central New York. IFW has received USCIS funding to enhance its Path to Citizenship education program and naturalization legal services in fiscal years 2012, 2017, and 2023. IFW has proposed it will serve 200 students and 200 naturalization applicants during the FY 2023 grant period.

organization_name: International Institute of Metropolitan St. Louis
description: Since its founding in 1919, International Institute of Metropolitan St. Louis (IISTL) has provided a variety of services to its foreign-born community. In 1980, IISTL established a robust ESL program and in 1983 it became a DOJ recognized agency. IISTL received its first USCIS grant in FY 2009. During the FY 2023 grant cycle, IISTL projects it will serve approximately 200 students and a minimum of 250 N-400s will be filed.

organization_name: Jewish Family and Vocational Service of Middlesex County, Inc.
description: As a USCIS grantee since 2010, Jewish Family and Vocation Service of Middlesex County (JFS) has continually offered citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to a growing audience. The LPR population JFS serves originates primarily from Latin America but also includes a growing number from India and Arabic-speaking nations. During the FY 2023 grant cycle, JFS will continue its robust citizenship education program offering nine classes that will enroll 390 LPRs, and they expect to submit 250 N-400s.

organization_name: Jewish Family Service of Western Massachusetts, Inc.
description: Jewish Family Service of Western Massachusetts (JFSWM) has provided citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to the Greater Springfield area for the last 13 years and has been a USCIS CINAS grantee for 10 of those years. With FY 2023 grant funding, JFSWM will provide citizenship instruction to 240 individuals and file a minimum of 240 Forms N-400.

La Casa de Don Pedro (LCDP) was founded in 1972 and first received USCIS funding in 2010. LCDP has provided citizenship instruction for over 20 years. In addition, LCDP has an established legal department that was created more than 20 years ago to counter the unlawful practice of immigration law plaguing their community. There is a high demand for naturalization 7 application services in the Newark metropolitan area. LCDP proposes to serve 200 individuals with citizenship instruction and naturalization application services for the FY 2023 grant cycle.

Laredo College is a higher education Hispanic-serving institution. The college received its first USCIS grant in FY 2021. It is a two-campus district serving the diverse needs of a growing community. Their two campuses serve more than 10,000 students each semester through a variety of affordable academic programs, technical and vocational programs, non-credit community interest courses, and adult education courses that help area adults obtain English skills, job skills or a General Educational Development diploma. For FY 2023, the program will enroll a minimum of 200 students who will apply for citizenship, and approximately 250 potential applicants will be recruited and screened for application services. Azteca Economic Development and Preservation Corporation will be subcontracted to provide naturalization application services.

For the FY 2023 grant cycle, Learning Empowered, Inc. will provide English language instruction, U.S. history and civics instruction, and naturalization application services to LPRs living in the Gulf Coast Region of Florida who wish to naturalize. Learning Empowered has successfully provided ESL services to approximately 465 immigrants annually over the past 22 years, and citizenship instruction services for the past 21 years to approximately 170 LPRs annually. Learning Empowered, Inc. first received a USCIS grant in FY 2013.

Literacy Network, in partnership with Centro Hispano, will offer comprehensive citizenship services, including citizenship instruction and naturalization application support, in Dane County, Wisconsin, to eligible LPRs. Literacy Network will provide citizenship instruction through group classes, equipping participants with the English language skills and knowledge needed for naturalization. At least 120 eligible individuals will participate in citizenship classes over the course of the FY 2023 grant cycle. Centro Hispano will provide naturalization application services. For the 2023 grant cycle, at least 120 individuals will receive naturalization eligibility screening and file Forms N-400 and G-28. The two agencies will collaborate to provide integrated services to best benefit program participants.

Lutheran Community Services Northwest (LCSNW) has provided services since 1921, naturalization application services for 37 years, and citizenship instruction for 21 years. Since the 1970s, LCSNW has provided low-cost immigration and legal services to immigrants and 8 refugees in Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas, Yamhill, and Marion counties. LCSNW first received grant funding from USCIS in FY 2010. Under the FY 2023 grant program, LCSNW will provide citizenship instruction to 250 LPRs and provide naturalization application services to 200 LPRs.

Lutheran Social Services and its sub-awardee, Community College of Aurora, will serve LPRs in the greater Denver and Aurora regions. These two organizations partner in The Denver and Aurora Citizenship Program (DACP). As experienced USCIS grant recipients, DACP will continue to provide high-quality citizenship instruction and naturalization legal services to approximately 200 diverse and underserved individuals with USCIS FY 2023 grant funding. LPRs served hail from 91 different countries with the majority originating from Mexico, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Burma/Myanmar, and Eritrea.

Make the Road New Jersey (MRNJ), a project of Make the Road States, supports immigrants to achieve dignity and respect through the provision of high-quality legal services and education programs. MRNJ has helped more than 1,000 immigrants become citizens through ESOL and civic instruction, naturalization test preparation, and N-400 application assistance since its founding in 2014. As a first-time USCIS CINAS grant recipient, MRNJ plans to enroll an additional 200 students and file an additional 200 Forms N-400 during the FY 2023 grant cycle.

organization_name: Michigan Organizing Project, dba Michigan United
description: Michigan Organizing Project, doing business as Michigan United, serves LPRs across the state of Michigan, specifically in Detroit, Grand Rapids, Kalamazoo, and Battle Creek. They provide low-cost immigration legal services to address immediate needs in the immigrant community. These needs include but are not limited to citizenship instruction, ESL classes, and assistance with naturalization applications. Through this grant, Michigan Organizing Project will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and naturalization application services to 200 LPRs.

Mid-Minnesota Legal Assistance (MMLA) has provided naturalization application services in the metro area of Minneapolis/St. Paul, MN, primarily Hennepin and Anoka Counties, including the City of Minneapolis, since 2001. MMLA's sub-awardee, Minneapolis Public Schools Adult Education (MPS-AE), is one of the largest Adult Basic Education programs in the state of Minnesota and has provided ESL instruction since 1977. MPS-AE has provided citizenship 9 instruction to the community since 1989. Through this grant, MMLA will provide naturalization application services to 180 LPRs and MPS-AE will provide citizenship instruction to 180 LPRs.

A recipient of the USCIS grants since FY 2010, Montgomery College has offered citizenship services since 2000. This proposed Citizenship Preparation Program will provide citizenship instruction and naturalization legal services to low and high beginning, and low intermediate English level LPRs. Anticipated outcomes include 320 eligible non-duplicated LPRs enrolled in grant-funded instruction, 320 LPRs who will receive naturalization eligibility screening, and 240 LPRs who will submit Forms N-400 and G-28. Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Washington, D.C., will serve as the sub-awardee. Additional programmatic goals include integration into the community, outreach, and N-400 workshop participation. The program will work with local libraries and Community Engagement Centers to enhance the community’s knowledge of naturalization services available through Montgomery College and USCIS.

Pars Equality Center has been providing immigration services since 2016. Pars Equality Center will serve lawful permanent residents residing in the Sherman Oaks and Irvine communities of Southern California. The Pars Equality Center was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2017. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, Pars Equality Center will provide citizenship instruction to 350 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 450 LPRs, and file 315 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Shorefront YM-YWHA of Brighton- Manhattan Beach, Inc.
description: Shorefront YM-YMHA (SY) has provided comprehensive citizenship instruction and naturalization application services as a USCIS grant recipient since 2011. SY serves one of the most ethnically diverse and densely populated areas of the country. For FY 2023, SY will serve 320 students and file a minimum of 520 Forms N-400.

organization_name: Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition
description: Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition (TIRRC) is a statewide immigrant and refugee-led nonprofit working to build a strong, welcoming, and inclusive Tennessee. Now in its 20th year, TIRRC is nationally recognized as a leader in bringing together organizations and individuals to build communities where immigrants and refugees can thrive. The funding from this opportunity will allow the TIRRC team to dedicate significant time and resources to providing citizenship preparation instruction and naturalization assistance services to 120 participants in each component. 10

organization_name: International Rescue Committee Inc., San Diego
description: The International Rescue Committee in San Diego (IRC-SD) has provided immigration services since 1975 to residents in San Diego County. Since 2012, they have provided ESL instruction. They will serve permanent residents that speak up to 45 non-English languages. IRC-SD was first awarded USCIS grant funding in FY 2011. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, IRC-SD will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 300 LPRs, and file 275 Forms N-400 and G-28.

For 45 years, the International Rescue Committee in Seattle (IRC-Seattle) has served immigrants, refugees, asylees, and victims of human trafficking from over 30 countries. IRC- Seattle has been a DOJ-recognized organization for more than 25 years and has provided citizenship education and ESL instruction since 1976. Under the FY 2023 grant cycle, IRC- Seattle will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and naturalization application services to 300 LPRs.

International Rescue Committee in Baltimore (IRC-Baltimore) and its partner, Baltimore Community College (BCCC), are the primary providers of naturalization application services and ESL instruction in the Baltimore metropolitan area. BCCC has 15 years of experience providing citizenship instruction, while IRC-Baltimore has been recognized by the DOJ since 2010. The Baltimore metropolitan area has 30% of Maryland’s LPRs. During the FY 2023 grant cycle, BCC has proposed to serve 250 newly enrolled students, while IRC projects it will submit a minimum of 250 Forms N-400.

organization_name: The School Board of Miami-Dade County, FL
description: The Fast Track to Citizenship VIII project will increase access to citizenship education for eligible LPRs in Miami-Dade County, Florida, by providing intensive citizenship education through the Miami-Dade County Public Schools (M-DCPS) Adult Education Program. M-DCPS has provided adult education for 62 years and is the largest provider in ESL and citizenship instruction in the State of Florida. In the past two years, M-DCPS has served approximately 38,000 ESL students. By partnering with Catholic Charities Legal Services (CCLS) of the Archdiocese of Miami, Inc., the Fast Track to Citizenship VIII project will provide naturalization application services to eligible students. CCLS has provided legal immigration services for more than 25 years, serving over 21,000 individuals in their community in the past two years. For the FY 2023 grant cycle, they will provide intensive citizenship instruction to 220 LPRs and naturalization application services for 220 LPRs. 11

Located in Fairfax County, Virginia, the primary goal of United Community Ministries is to end generational poverty by addressing and removing barriers from families. The organization will use USCIS funding to increase their capacity to serve an additional 120 LPRs, with expanded two-tiered services in citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to gain the knowledge and skills necessary to assimilate successfully into their community.

organization_name: Up Valley Family Centers of Napa County
description: Since 2016, Up Valley Family Centers of Napa County has provided immigration services. It will serve lawful permanent residents from primarily Spanish-speaking countries residing in northern Napa County, California. Up Valley Family Centers of Napa County was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2023. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, Up Valley Family Centers of Napa County will provide citizenship instruction to 120 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 120 LPRs, and file 120 Forms N-400 and G-28.

US Together’s immigrant community is primarily composed of Somalis, Bhutanese- Nepalis and Latin Americans. It has provided ESL instruction since 2005 and citizenship instruction since 2011. During the FY 2023 grant cycle, US Together will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and naturalization application services to 200 LPRs.

Women for Afghan Women (WAW) first received USCIS funding in FY 2019. WAW and the Jacob A. Riis Neighborhood Settlement (Riis) will continue their partnership for the FY 2023 CINAS grant cycle to provide 200 clients with citizenship instruction and immigration legal services. Sixty percent of WAW’s clients are Afghans, but it also serves the diverse immigrant communities primarily in Queens, NY.

This organization received USCIS grant funding between FY 2012 and FY 2019 and resumed in FY 2021. The YMCA of Greater Houston will continue to serve LPR’s eligible to apply for naturalization by providing citizenship instruction, naturalization eligibility screening, and N-400 12 application preparation to 200 individuals. They will focus primarily on underserved permanent residents, who traditionally have greater barriers to achieving naturalization. 13 Community and Regional Integration Network Grant (CARING)

Solutions in Hometown Connections (SHC) and sub-awardee, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA), have partnered to provide citizenship instruction and naturalization application services to LPRs in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties in Maryland as well as in Arlington, Alexandria, and Prince William counties in Virginia. LSSNCA has met the changing needs of its community since 1917, while SHC has connected with vulnerable and isolated members of the immigrant community since its inception in 2017. SHC is also partnering with the Prince George’s County Library to provide physical space for classes and complementary educational programs for English language learners, such as digital literacy. Together the organizations plan to serve 180 vulnerable immigrants during the FY 2023 grant cycle. 14 Innovations in Citizenship Preparation (Innovations)

Founded in 2006, Amistades proposes “Movemineto Ollin” as an innovative and replicable new approach to engaging and supporting LPRs from Mexico living along Arizona’s southern corridor toward naturalization and citizenship. The project will work to reach eligible LPRs who have not pursued naturalization. Amistades will specifically focus on those who have jobs that require mobility and/or non-traditional hours of operation and live in the most rural areas of the region.

Founded in 2010, the Arkansas United Community Coalition (Arkansas United) is Arkansas’ first and only statewide immigrant rights advocacy and civic engagement organization. Arkansas United's proposed citizenship preparation initiative, the Together Towards Citizenship (TTC) Program, is aimed at understanding and addressing the needs of LPRs in Arkansas, ultimately facilitating their path towards citizenship. With USCIS FY 2023 grant funding, the TTC program will engage in pioneering data collection methods and focus groups in targeted communities with high immigrant populations, designed to gather essential information with the goal of providing personalized assistance to individuals and connecting them with established naturalization resources and professionals.

CASA has served immigrant communities since 1985. CASA’s innovation is a new “Citizenship Corps” outreach and wrap-around services model coupled with a new, no-code software tool to serve LPRs. Upon completion of the innovation, CASA will be able to identify LPRs in spaces frequented in their regular daily lives, screen for eligibility, link identified LPRs to service providers, and assist LPRs filing Forms N-400.

organization_name: Catholic Charities Community Services Archdiocese of NY
description: Catholic Charities Community Services Archdiocese of NY (CCCS of NY) will target low- income LPRs who experience barriers to citizenship such as lacking English proficiency and/or confidence in their skills, lacking an understanding of the administrative requirements and the digital proficiency required to file their citizenship applications, or those who may have legal questions about their applications that prevent them from moving forward. CCCS of NY will address these challenges by providing flexible, responsive support to their students so this 15 population of LPRs can move forward in the naturalization process in a more informed, empowered, and proactive way. The areas to be served will be Bronx County, Rockland County, Orange County, and Dutchess County in New York State.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Miami, Inc.
description: Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Miami (CCADM) “Innovations in Citizenship Project” will establish a mobile citizenship clinic to bring citizenship preparation services directly to low- income LPRs at local community sites. The mobile unit will work with Spanish and Haitian Creole speaking LPRs. This will include case management, legal services and citizenship instruction. CCADM will partner with faith-based organizations, schools, community centers, residential facilities, and other sites that frequently serve immigrants and LPRs, and utilize partnerships to provide comprehensive wrap-around services for citizenship preparation. Case management and immigration legal services will be available to LPRs to assist in overcoming financial barriers to applying for citizenship. Citizenship instruction will also be available on-site or virtually through an implementation partner.

Founded in 2017, Greater Portland Immigrant Welcome Center proposes “Preparing Maine’s Senior Immigrants for Citizenship,” a comprehensive outreach, client evaluation and citizenship program for senior Maine immigrants who are LPRs. This represents a major step forward for the Greater Portland Immigrant Welcome Center, establishing it as an institutional provider of comprehensive citizenship and integration services alongside other programs including English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL), food security, workforce readiness and entrepreneurship programs.

The Hispanic Federation (HF) proposes a Motivational Citizenship Academy for an innovative project focused on reaching long-term LPRs in North Carolina. Between 2010 and 2020, North Carolina’s Hispanic population grew by nearly 320,000, the largest numeric increase of any racial/ethnic group in the state, with faster growth in rural areas. The short-term goal of the project is to encourage LPRs hesitant to apply for citizenship to start the naturalization process by providing education and public awareness at the grassroots level.

The National Immigration Forum (NIF) will offer an innovative citizenship education program complete with an original civics English curriculum aligned to the new naturalization test requirements, live instruction, online digital learning, practice for the interview and test, and 16 personalized support. The project will consist of blended training that combines 50% live instruction from trained educators with 50% independent online learning to build civics English skills and digital literacy. While the program will prepare eligible LPRs for the citizenship test, it specifically focuses on developing a curriculum to support applicants with low literacy and low- English proficiency. To reach populations with historically limited access to quality citizenship preparation services, NIF will leverage its existing faith and business networks, and focus on the following states: Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, South Dakota, and Texas.

Open Arms Community Center Corp (Open Arms) proposes to develop high-quality English as a Second Language and Civics (ESL/Civics) citizenship preparation services program delivered by an ESL-certified instructor in a real-time instruction video accessible through computer or smart phone platforms. Open Arms’ design is intended to encompass the need of LPRs who have barriers to high-quality instruction services due to residing in rural locations or other isolated areas where there is a lack of access to citizenship education services and/or whose jobs require mobility or have an inconsistent work schedule. The real-time video will engage students to be able to feel part of a class and the ESL instructor will be able to monitor student progress and provide feedback on each section covered.

Queens Borough Public Library proposes an innovative citizenship education program that addresses the specific barriers faced by mothers and working individuals who are seeking citizenship instruction. Queens Borough Public Library’s planned innovation is an integration of multiple program components to increase eligible legal permanent residents’ access, retention, and success in a citizenship education program. These components are childcare support, a digital literacy bootcamp, hybrid learning with flexibly scheduled in-person classes, a project- based curriculum, and case management support. Queens Borough Public Library will research, develop, and test a mix of program components as part of a pilot citizenship instruction program over the two-year grant period.

The Genesis Center has served low-moderate income Rhode Islanders for over 40 years. More recently, as a member of the Rhode Island Citizenship Consortium, The Genesis Center has been successful in educating and preparing LPRs to successfully pass their citizenship exam. Since 2018, they have helped 235 students become U.S. citizens. The Genesis Center proposes to design and implement a contextualized English class focusing on holistic integration into systems of American prosperity. The Genesis Center will focus on barriers that preclude immigrants from fully engaging with government services and will focus on the role that digital literacy and digital navigation plays in this component. 17

Founded in 2014, Immigrant Connection proposes an in-person, low-cost citizenship preparation and immigration legal services program for rural immigrants where citizenship services may be non-existent, severely limited, or very far distances away. With USCIS FY 2023 funding, Immigrant Connection aims to provide a direct pathway for LPRs in the rural areas of North Carolina, Indiana, Mississippi, and Iowa who may struggle to overcome the many barriers to naturalization.

The Utah Citizenship Initiative, led by the Utah Governor’s Office of Economic Opportunity’s Center for Immigration & Integration, is a three-pronged approach to promote, educate, and connect on naturalization and citizenship preparation to reduce barriers preventing LPRs from accessing legal services and applying for citizenship. This initiative will promote greater civic participation and engagement among naturalized citizens in rural communities and strengthen social cohesion and integration between immigrants and the broader community. This innovative approach seeks to provide a road map for other states to follow to increase the rates of naturalization utilizing a hybrid model of virtual citizenship education classes, coupled with naturalization legal services. 18

The Ansob Center for Refugees (Ansob Center) has been providing immigration services since 2000. It will serve permanent residents from Arabic- and French-speaking countries in Africa and the Middle East residing in Astoria, Queens, New York. The Ansob Center was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2011. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, the Ansob Center will provide citizenship instruction to 200 lawful permanent residents (LPRs), administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 416 LPRs, and file 400 Forms N-400 and G-28.

The Asian Community & Cultural Center (ACCC), along with partner and sub-awardee El Centro de las Américas (ECDLA), will use their combined 38 years of citizenship education experience to provide citizenship instruction. In partnership with Lutheran Family Services and Catholic Social Services, ACCC will provide legal assistance for LPRs. ACCC was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2020. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, ACCC and its partners will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs and naturalization application services to 200 LPRs – with a focus on Karen, Karenni, Sudanese, Kurdish, Afghan, Arabi Iraqi, and Yezidi LPRs.

organization_name: Asian Pacific Development Center of Colorado
description: The Asian Pacific Development Center (APDC) and sub-awardee, Catholic Charities of Denver (CCD) have partnered to create an integrated continuum of instruction and application services to assist community members in obtaining citizenship. APDC offers whole-health, integrated care services from pre-literacy classes to post-naturalization workshops. APDC has provided ESL services since 2003 and citizenship classes since 2010. APDC’s current programs reach over 1,000 students annually, and in FY 20-21, instructional hours reached 75,205. CCD assists clients in and around the Denver metropolitan area and provides services across the archdiocese, which encompasses all of northern Colorado from Rifle to Yuma. Clients unable to travel to Denver receive services virtually. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, APDC and CCD will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

BakerRipley’s Immigration & Citizenship Program (the Program) was established in 2006 to serve the Houston region’s LPRs and the immigrant community. The Program connects individuals to ESL- Citizenship classes, naturalization application assistance, classroom-based naturalization test prep, and prep for the USCIS interview - in a seamless, integrated sequence. Since 2008, BakerRipley has provided naturalization application services through direct legal representation and large-scale application assistance workshops under the guidance of attorneys and DOJ reps. First funded by USCIS in FY 2015, Baker-Ripley serves clients from over 15 different countries including Mexico, Honduras, and El Salvador. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, BakerRipley will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 640 LPRs, and file 210 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Boat People SOS-Houston (BPSOS) has been providing naturalization application services since 2004 and citizenship instruction since 2009 throughout the greater Houston area – with a focus on helping Vietnamese and other Asians LPRs overcome multiple barriers to achieving citizenship. BPSOS was first awarded a USCIS grant under the FY 2010 National Capacity Building Grant Program. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, BPSOS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Charities Diocese of Forth Worth
description: Catholic Charities Diocese of Fort Worth (CCFW) has provided the Fort Worth immigrant community with ESL classes since 1992 and with immigration legal services since 1983. CCFW was first awarded a USCIS grant in FY 2010. CCFW’s LPR citizenship classes, which feature ESL instruction, and CCFW’s Immigrant Consultation Services (ICS) have supported immigrants from more than 22 countries. Many students are seniors and/or refugees; clients are often economically disadvantaged and possess low levels of literacy, education, and English proficiency. CCFW is the only naturalization services provider that addresses the needs of individuals located in rural areas surrounding Tarrant County. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, CCFW will provide citizenship instruction to 250 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 350 LPRs, and file 300 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Catholic Charities of Dallas (CCD) has over 40 years of experience providing English language education and naturalization services to immigrants in North Texas. CCD has delivered citizenship instruction since the mid-1990s and was one of the first organizations to be awarded a USCIS grant under this program in FY 2009. Given that approximately 25% of eligible-to-naturalize LPRs in the state are within CCD’s service area, CCD anticipates serving permanent residents from a wide variety of countries, including Mexico, El Salvador, Burma, Bhutan, Ethiopia, Burundi, Dem Rep of Congo, and Iraq. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, CCD will provide citizenship instruction to 300 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 500 LPRs, and file 300 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Catholic Charities Diocese of Rochester’s Catholic Charities Family and Community Services (CCFCS) has served the Greater Rochester community since 1917. CCFCS has been administrating citizenship programming including ESL/Civics instruction and naturalization assistance consistently since 2013 and was awarded its first USCIS grant in FY 2015. The presence of many refugees and immigrants in Rochester and the Finger Lakes area drives the continued need for Citizenship and Integration Services provided by CCFCS. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, CCFCS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 280 LPRs, and file 240 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Stockton
description: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Stockton (CCDS) has provided citizenship and naturalization application assistance for more than 10 years to low-income, lawful permanent residents (LPRs) in San Joaquin and Stanislaus Counties to promote citizenship achievement and community assimilation. CCDS was awarded its first USCIS grant in FY 2011 and has been recognized as a USCIS grantee success story for innovation and commitment to clients. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, CCDS will provide citizenship instruction to 240 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 400 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

organization_name: Catholic Community Services of Southern Arizona
description: Catholic Community Services of Southern Arizona (CCS) and sub-awardee Adult Basic Education for College and Career Division (ABECC) of Pima Community College will provide seamless, comprehensive citizenship acquisition services throughout Southeastern Arizona. ABECC has been providing citizenship instruction in Tucson, AZ, since 1997 and will handle the citizenship education component. CCS will provide naturalization services and lead the effort. CCS has provided naturalization application assistance to low-income new Americans for close to 40 years and has decades of history working with ABECC. With USCIS FY 2022 funding, CCS will provide citizenship instruction to 200 LPRs, administer naturalization eligibility screenings to 200 LPRs, and file 200 Forms N-400 and G-28.

Catholic Migration Services (CMS) has been providing naturalization application services since its founding in 1971. CMS will partner with LaGuardia Community College’s Center for Immigrant Education & Training (LGCC), which has more than 10 years of experience providing citizenship instruction. CMS, with LGCC as sub-awardee, was first awarded USCIS grant funds in FY 2014.
